chunks: We enjoined upon man to be good to his parents; his mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning is thirty months, until when he reaches maturity and reaches forty years, he says: 'My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve, and make good for me in my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of gratitude for parents mentioned in the Quran at the age of forty?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this verse is pivotal for establishing the thirty-month period of gestation and weaning, often cited in fiqh and hadith to define the complete developmental stage before adulthood. It highlights the transition from parental care to individual accountability, emphasizing that gratitude (shukr) to God is intrinsically linked to kindness (ihsan) toward parents. The supplication of the forty-year-old serves as a model for mature believers seeking divine assistance to fulfill their duties and secure righteousness for their progeny.
